tossups.text: In a play from this country, a group of villagers kills the Commander, and when tortured, residents only say that the title village did it. In another play from this country, a Polish prince is locked in a tower and convinced by his father that a brief episode of freedom is just a dream. An author from this country wrote a play in which Death is disguised as a beggar and Leonardo runs off with the Bride before he and the Groom kill each other. Life is a Dream and Blood Wedding are plays from, for 10 points, what country home to Pedro Calderón de la Barca, Lope de Vega, and Federico García Lorca?

This ocean includes the Cocos or Keeling Islands. On another island in this ocean in 2018, John Allen Chau was killed while trying to serve as a missionary to the Sentinelese. This ocean includes the Gulf of Khambhat and the Meghna River delta which are, respectively, part of the Arabian Sea and Bay of Bengal found on opposite sides of the country that shares its name with this ocean. For 10 points, name this ocean between Africa and Australia.

Unusually, this substance has a solid-liquid boundary with a negative slope on its phase diagram. Specific gravity is defined as the ratio of the density of any substance to the density of this substance, which is about one gram per milliliter. This substance's high surface tension and adhesive forces allow it to travel up the xylem of plants through a process known as capillary action. For ten points, name this "universal solvent" that, when cooled below 32 degrees Fahrenheit, becomes ice.

Majid Rahnema claimed that this concept served to 'strengthen the structures that generate poverty'. James Ferguson analysed the 'unintended consequences' of this concept in a work that examines the bureaucratic power in one country. That work, called the Anti-Politics Machine, asks 'what do programs [involving this concept] do besides fail poor people?'. William Easterly critiqued a work by Jeffrey Sachs by arguing that this policy was implemented by ineffective 'planners' in The White Man's Burden. That work by Sachs advocates this policy as a means of accomplishing the title goal in The End of Poverty. For 10 points, name this voluntary transfer of resources from one country to another.

In both of these two countries, a football chant was co-opted into a slogan denouncing a political leader as a "dickhead." The colloquial term "little green men" refers to masked soldiers in one of these two countries armed with military equipment provided by the other. One of these two countries routinely demonizes the far-right wing Right Sector party in the other. One of these two countries issued passports to members of the secret police force Berkut after it was dissolved by the other country. Both of these two countries have been blamed for shooting down Malaysian Airlines Flight 17 during their ongoing war in the region of Donbass. For 10 points, name these two countries whose relationship soured when one annexed Crimea from the other.
acceptableAnswers: accept answers listing the countries in either order

tossups.text: One character in this work takes biannual vacations to Civil War battlefields. Another character in this work becomes valedictorian of his class at MIT only to die in World War I. Its second section ends with a marriage between George and Emily, the latter of whom dies during childbirth in this work's last act, "Death." Beginning on May 7th, 1901, this work takes place in Grover's Corners, New Hampshire and is narrated by a Stage Manager. For 10 points, identify this play focusing on the Webb and Gibbs families, written by Thornton Wilder.

Two of these objects sit near the town of Quauhnahuac, where a British consul lives in Mexico, in a breakout novel of Malcolm Lowry set Under them. A maar can form near one of these objects, whose distinctive types include the tuya. Pliny the Elder died while attempting to return from one of these structures. In 2009, money spent to watch these objects was criticized by Bobby Jindal's State of the Union response. Asteroid B-612 has three of these structures, which the Little Prince cleans each day. These structures can produce pahoehoe and 'a'a. For 10 points, name these geologic structures whose shield and cinder cone types can produce lava.

The Spitzer telescope operates in this range of the light spectrum. This region of light is used in spectroscopy to measure vibrating bonds. William Herschel discovered this non-visible type of light from the sun by measuring its heating ability. For 10 points, name this region of electromagnetic radiation used in night vision goggles and thermal imaging that, unlike ultraviolet light, has longer wavelengths than visible light.

The state office regulating these structures during the Tang dynasty, called the Zhenguan-shu ("zhung-wen shoo"), was modeled on a similar set up by the Western Jin. The oldest example of these structures in China are six of them that were found in the type site of the Yangshao culture, a village named Banpo. In 2011 a horseshoe-shaped design of these structures called "steamed-bun" or mantou ("mahn-toe") was successfully recreated. A Japanese design of these structures called anagama is based on the steep-sloped "dragon" style of them invented in China, which takes advantage of countercurrent exchange. Since around 300 A.D. a bunch of these structures have operated in the city Jingdezhen ("jing-duh-zhen") and given that city its fame. A type of ware named for some of these structures at Yue represents the earliest mass-produced celadon. For 10 points, name these structures which heat and bake pottery.

This ruler was severely challenged by a revolt led by Spitamenes in Sogdiana after this man had captured Bessus. However, his other plans, such as improving the irrigation of the Euphrates and settling the Persian Gulf were cut short by his premature death. While he had a son with the Princess Roxana, after his death his generals tore apart his empire in the Wars of the Diadochi. The victor at the battles of Gaugamela and Issus over Darius III, For 10 points, name this Macedonian who conquered the Persian Empire.

Three albums on Nonesuch Records by Joshua Rifkin helped to revive interest in this style during the 1970s. The "Graceful Ghost" is among the dozens of pieces William Bolcom has written in this style. A song whose title mentions this style asks "if you want to hear 'Swanee River' played in" this style; that song was an Irving Berlin hit about a "Band" led by "Alexander" that performed it. Joseph Lamb and James Scott were among the "Big Three" composers in this genre, as was the composer of the opera Treemonisha. Cakewalks are often considered a precursor to this genre due to their shared syncopation and origins in African-American music. "The Entertainer" is a piece in, for 10 points, what genre pioneered by Scott Joplin?

This politician began one speech with the metaphor of a mariner on an "unknown sea." This man likely lost a political position due to a speech where he spoke as an "American" and not a man from his home state. This author of the 7th of March speech declared "Liberty and Union, now and forever, one and inseparable" in a rebuttal to Robert Hayne. With John C. Calhoun and Henry Clay, this Senator formed the "Great Triumvirate." This Senator negotiated a border treaty with Lord Ashburton in 1842. For 10 points, name this Senator from Massachusetts, who shares his name with a famous English language dictionary.

The winning side of this battle had its main position at Henry House Hill. The losing side was led by General Irvin McDowell. General Joseph Johnston rushed reinforcements to P. G.T Beauregard at this battle. General Bernard Bee was shot at this battle after proclaiming, "There stands Jackson like a stone wall!" For 10 points, name this first major battle of the Civil War.

The CIA may have attempted to assassinate this man using poisoned cigars during Operation Mongoose. After a failed attack on the Moncada Barracks, this man defended himself in the "History Will Absolve Me" speech. This man led the 26th of July Movement during a guerilla war in which he overthrew Fulgencio Batista. This man stepped down as his country's leader in 2008 and gave power to his brother Raul. For ten points, name this longtime Communist president of Cuba.

In human physiology, this structure is essential for white blood cell types. It plays a key role in the cardiovascular system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this erythrocyte-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The erythrocyte is a key component of the Cardiovascular system, involved in white blood cell types.

tossups.text: Abbé Faria was imprisoned for proposing a unified Italy and dies of catalepsy in this work, whose protagonist once disguises himself as a clerk from Thomson and French in Rome to save Morrel. Noitier reveals a plot to murder Valentine to Villefort, and the protagonist's manipulation of the bond market wipes out Danglars's fortunes. Seeing the protagonist completing his revenge for imprisonment in the Chateau d'If and the loss of Mercedes, for 10 points, identify this novel by Alexandre Dumas.

A woman in this play is criticized by her boyfriend Joseph Asagai [AH-suh-"guy"] for straightening her hair, which he believes is "mutilation." In this play, Willy runs off with another character's life insurance money to purchase a liquor store. This play centers on Karl Lindner's attempts to bribe a family not to move to the all-white Clybourne Park neighborhood of Chicago. For ten points, name this play about the Younger family written by Lorraine Hansberry.

This title place is shown in a bright pink and purple landscape painted in 1927 Marsden Hartley, who greatly admired another artist who painted it for his way of establishing the "quality of reality." Another artist first showed this place in the right background of his landscape The Railway Cutting. This place is alluded to as the location where that artist spent "entire days...reading Virgil and looking at the sky" in a review by Paul Gauguin. The trees in front of this place are painted using cubes and other increasingly abstract forms in works painted closer to that artist's 1906 death. Using shades and techniques similar to those found in his Basket of Apples an artist depicted this place at different angles and times of the day while living in Aix-en-Provence. For 10 points, name this mountain frequently depicted by Paul Cezanne.

This anatomical structure, studied extensively in clinical medicine, this structure is essential for duodenum, jejunum, ileum. It plays a key role in the digestive system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this duodenum-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The duodenum is a key component of the Digestive system, involved in duodenum, jejunum, ileum.

tossups.text: In this government, André Tulard was in charge of the distribution of yellow badges, an action connected with a group led by Xavier Vallet. This government's agenda in North Africa was promulgated by the admiral Jean Darlan, who was assassinated by Bonnier de la Chapelle. It held the Vel'd'hiv raids, which sent people to the Drancy camp, and ran under the motto of "Work, Family, Fatherland". It supplanted the Third Republic and was led by the hero of Verdun, Philippe Pétain. For 10 points, name this puppet government instituted in France by the Nazi state.

parts.text: This author wrote of the six-sunned planet Kalgash in Nightfall, as well as penning I, Robot and the Foundation series. His recurring character R. Daneel Olivaw created a "Zeroth Law" to add to this author's 3 Laws of Robotics.
This author won the first Nebula award for his novel Dune, which tells of Paul Atreides rise to power on the spice-mining planet of Arrakis.
This man borrowed a line from Exodus to title his Stranger in a Strange Land, in which Valentine Michael Smith returns from Mars and finds out he is heir to the Lyle Drive fortune.

bonuses.leadin: Name the following science-fiction writers, for 10 points each:

parts.text: The Tower Bridge crosses over this river, as well as the Millenium Bridge, which links the Globe Theatre to St. Paul's Cathedral. Cities on this river include Oxford, Windsor, and Reading.

This third-longest river in Italy rises from Mount Fumaiolo and flows through Umbria and Lazio to the Tyrrhenian Sea. Bridges across it include the Ponte Sant'Angelo, built in 134 AD by Emperor Hadrian.

Arising in the Albarracin Mountains in Spain, this river flows through Toledo and supplies drinking water to Madrid before forming the boundary between Portugal and Spain and then emptying into the Atlantic Ocean at Lisbon.

bonuses.leadin: Identify the following rivers that flow through European capitals, for 10 points each.

parts.text: Name this organ, the major component of the integumentary system. The epidermis is the outermost layer of this organ.
The skin contains follicles for these thin protein filaments, which are found most abundantly on the head and can be brushed with a comb.
Hair and fingernails are both abundant in this tough protein. 95% of the epidermis consists of cells that make this protein.

bonuses.leadin: This human organ has the largest surface area. For 10 points each:

parts.text: This mood conveys commands or requests.
Depending on the language this mood can convey possibility, necessity, and desire.
This mood conveys a request or suggestion.

bonuses.leadin: 20. Identify the grammatical mood being described FTPE.

parts.text: The French Revolution basically spelled the end for this medieval system after the nobility lost rights given by the old Manor System. It is based on holding land in fee and involved lords, vassals, and fiefs.
On June 20th, 1789, members of this lowest social order signed the Tennis Court Oath. This order was distinguished from the higher nobility and clergy, and made up most of the population.
The National Assembly ran into this problem after issuing the assignat. In 1923. the Rentenmark was issued in order to combat this problem in the Weimar Republic.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, name these non-violent aspects of the French Revolution:

parts.text: Name this writer who spent almost her entire life in Amherst, Massachusetts.
In one Dickinson poem, this character "kindly stopped for" the speaker because she "could not stop for" him.
One Dickinson poem ends with the line "I could not see to see." In that work, the speaker claims to hear what animal when she dies?

bonuses.leadin: This poet wrote "I Like to See It Lap the Miles". For 10 points each:

parts.text: One process used to purify crude is this process, a method of separation based on the differences in boiling points of a mixture.
This is one fractional distillate of petroleum, specifically the cut between 250 and 300oC. Equivalent to number two fuel oil, it is denser than gasoline.
Another important refining operation is this process where complex hydrocarbons are converted to lighter molecules. Varieties of this process include fluid catalytic, thermal, steam, and hydro.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, identify each of the following about the chemistry of gasoline.

parts.text: Name these types of organisms which absorb nutrients from decaying matter . More common examples of these organisms consist of earthworms which consume detritus.
Some xylophagus fungi evolved with the ability to digest lignin found in this material. Termites can digest this material which is found in the bark of trees.
Soft-rot fungi secrete an enzyme that can digest this glucose polymer found in plant cell walls.

bonuses.leadin: Saprotrophic fungi are an example of this kind of organism. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this state whose government was protested heavily by teachers after Governor Scott Walker proposed the elimination of most collective bargaining rights for unions.
This pair of brothers raised eyebrows by donating heavily to Walker's campaign. David founded Citizens for a Sound Economy and Charles cofounded the Cato institute.

This political advocacy group split off from Citizens for a Sound Economy in 2004. Obama named it as one of the "shadowy groups with harmless sounding names," and its agents were criticized for plastering fake eviction notices on Detroit homes in June of 2011.

bonuses.leadin: In June of 2011, a dispute arose in this state's Supreme Court over whether or not Justice David Prosser choked Justice Ann Walsh Bradley. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this American general who followed up a victory over Black Kettle at Washita River with a crushing defeat at the hands of the Sioux at Little Big Horn.
This Sioux leader became overall chieftain in 1867 and led the native forces at Little Big Horn after having a vision of US soldiers falling like grasshoppers into the camp.

This was the Cavalry regiment led by Custer which was crushed at Little Big Horn. This unit is known as the "Garryowen," conducted the Black Hills Expedition, and captured Chief Joseph after the Battle of Bear Paw.

bonuses.leadin: During the Civil War he led the Michigan Brigade, which was sometimes known as his "wolverines." For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this sixteen-year-old artist from New Zealand, whose singles include "Tennis Court" and one that begins "I've never seen a diamond in the flesh."
That single by Lorde is this song that advocates against lavish lifestyles in its chorus: "that kind of luxe just ain't for us / we crave a different kind of buzz."
"Tennis Court" and "Royals" appear in this debut album by Lorde.

bonuses.leadin: The chorus of one song by this artist begins "Baby be the class clown/ I'll be the beauty queen in tears." For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this region, now in northern France, whose first Scandinavian duke took control here 175 years before a descendant commissioned the Domesday (dooms-day) Book.
France reconquered Normandy from England at this war's Battle of Formigny (FOR-meen-yee). Henry V (the fifth) was victorious in this war's Battle of Agincourt (AH-jin-kor).
This Viking, who was baptized as Robert I (the first), was the first Duke of Normandy. He often clashed with Charles the Simple.

bonuses.leadin: William Longsword succeeded a duke of this region who acquired it in the Treaty of Saint-Clair-sur-Epte (SAH-klair-soor-EP-tuh). For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this alloy, primarily made with copper and tin, that was used throughout the ancient world to make weapons and tools.
This weapon became an extremely popular bronze weapon for warriors. Bronze's strength allowed for smiths to create this weapon with a longer blade than daggers or knives.
These Greek soldiers used bronze shields, called hoplons, which are the origin of their name. These soldiers often entered battle in organized formations called phalanxes.

bonuses.leadin: This metal alloy was used by cultures like Hyksos, Assyrians, and the Middle Kingdom of Egypt. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this hunter and Pony Express rider who made his fortune with a namesake Wild West Show which toured Europe, entertaining aristocrats with cowboy and indian-themed shows.
One member of Buffalo Bill's Wild West Show was this noted female sharpshooter and wife of Frank Butler, who later became the subject of a musical by Irving Berlin.
Another famous member of the Wild West Show was this former Sioux chief whose vision of defeating cavalry before the Battle of Little Bighorn inspired the Native American warriors during that clash.

bonuses.leadin: While serving as a civilian scout for the U.S. Cavalry, this man received a Medal of Honor which was later revoked because he really didn't deserve it in the first place. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name the primary structure associated with duodenum, jejunum, ileum.
What is the main function of the duodenum in the digestive system?
Name another component of the digestive system related to duodenum, jejunum, ileum.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, answer these questions about the human digestive system.

parts.text: This poet asked, "those who are beautiful, oh who can retain them?" in the second of his ten Duino Elegies. The line, "Breathe, invisible poem!" appears in the 27th of his 55 Sonnets to Orpheus.
This polymath wrote about a man's unhappy reaction to Lotte and Albert's marriage in The Sorrows of Young Werther and a play about a scholar's deal with Satan, Faust.

Cipolla and Silvestra's boyfriend are the two title characters of this author's short story "Mario and the Magician." He also wrote about the writer Gustav von Aschenbach in his novella Death in Venice.

bonuses.leadin: Name these people who wrote in the German language, for 10 points each.

parts.text: Name this Cockney flower girl, who Professor Higgins attempts to teach "proper manners" in a bet with Colonel Pickering.
Eliza appears in Pygmalion, a play by this Irish playwright who also wrote about the anarchist John Tanner confronting the conservative Ann Whitefield in Man and Superman.

The oft-separately-performed Act Three of Man and Superman features the main characters having a conversation with this figure "in Hell." An epic poem by Lord Byron mocking this figure is considered commentary on the decline of Spain.

bonuses.leadin: This character stuns Freddy Eynsford-Hill when she shouts "not bloody likely!" in response to being asked for a walk in the Coventry Gardens. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this photograph that is a parody of and shares its name with a Grant Wood painting.
Gordon Parks contributed many photographs to this magazine, whose photographers when it launched in 1936 included Alfred Eisenstaedt, Thomas McAvoy, and Peter Stackpole.
The cover photo for the first issue of Life was by this woman, who also took a famous photo of Gandhi at his spinning wheel and provided photos for the book You Have Seen Their Faces.

bonuses.leadin: This photograph from 1942 depicts Ella Watson, a janitor at the Farm Security Administration, holding a broom and mop in front of a flag, and was taken by Gordon Parks. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name the primary structure associated with hepatic portal system.
What is the main function of the liver in the digestive system?
Name another component of the digestive system related to hepatic portal system.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, answer these questions about the human digestive system.

parts.text: Name this state, whose 1876 election saw mass political violence that included the Hamburg Massacre. Red Shirts member Ben Tillman later became its governor and senator in his own right.

All of that happened in this era of U.S. history, which followed the Civil War. This era, which was "redeemed" by Jim Crow Laws, spawned white terrorist groups like the White Knights in Louisiana, as well as the KKK.

The KKK drastically weakened this government agency, which was formed to help freed slaves. Oliver Howard directed this agency, which opened up thousands of schools and HBCUs before being closed by Ulysses S. Grant.

bonuses.leadin: In this state, the white supremacist Red Shirts used violence to help elect governor Wade Hampton. For 10 points each:
